chapters.title: The Gap Nobody Knows
chapters.sourcePressure: Diagnostic opening: execution is the missing link between aspirations and results, belongs to leaders, and has to live in culture through what is inspected, rewarded, and tolerated.
chapters.coreMove: Turn a declared ambition into a reality-tested operating path before treating it as a real plan.
chapters.commonMisread: Make execution sound like generic accountability or post-strategy effort.

chapters.title: The Execution Difference
chapters.sourcePressure: Contrast chapter: Xerox and Lucent mark execution loss, EDS marks stronger execution, and the useful lesson is how operating truth travels before final results collapse.
chapters.coreMove: Read execution quality from early truth-flow signals instead of waiting for the scoreboard.
chapters.commonMisread: Turn named companies into unsupported case-study theater or business trivia.

chapters.title: Building Block One: The Leader's Seven Essential Behaviors
chapters.sourcePressure: First building block: execution becomes concrete through seven leader behaviors, from knowing people and the business to realism, priorities, follow-through, doer rewards, coaching, self-knowledge, and emotional fortitude.
chapters.coreMove: Convert leadership intent into visible behaviors that make realism and follow-through unavoidable.
chapters.commonMisread: Summarize leadership traits as personality advice detached from execution.

chapters.title: Building Block Two: Creating the Framework for Cultural Change
chapters.sourcePressure: Second building block: culture changes through operational consequences, rewards tied to performance, social software, robust dialogue, and the behavior leaders exhibit or tolerate.
chapters.coreMove: Redesign the consequences and conversations that teach people what the culture really values.
chapters.commonMisread: Treat culture as slogans, values statements, or morale work.

chapters.title: Building Block Three: The Job No Leader Should Delegate
chapters.sourcePressure: Third building block: getting the right people in the right jobs is non-delegable because comfort, weak knowledge, and lack of courage keep mismatches alive.
chapters.coreMove: Face role fit directly enough to move the right person into the work the strategy actually needs.
chapters.commonMisread: Turn people decisions into generic hiring tips or harsh performance-management talk.

chapters.title: The People Process
chapters.sourcePressure: Core process one: the people process must link people to strategy and operations through pipeline depth, succession, retention risk, nonperformance, HR linkage, and candid dialogue.
chapters.coreMove: Make talent review answer the business plan instead of sitting beside it as a separate ritual.
chapters.commonMisread: Make this an HR process chapter about forms and annual reviews.

chapters.title: The Strategy Process
chapters.sourcePressure: Core process two: strategy has to explain the hows and test external environment, customers, markets, competition, executable capability, milestones, time balance, critical issues, and sustainable economics.
chapters.coreMove: Cross-examine a strategy until the how, capability, milestones, and economics are visible.
chapters.commonMisread: Treat strategy as a polished destination statement or framework exercise.

chapters.title: How to Conduct a Strategy Review
chapters.sourcePressure: Strategy review: the meeting has to pressure the plan through questions about competition, capability, focus, idea choice, people linkage, operations linkage, and follow-through.
chapters.coreMove: Run a strategy review that changes the plan by forcing sharper questions and commitments.
chapters.commonMisread: Make the review a polite presentation, status meeting, or critique session.

chapters.title: The Operations Process
chapters.sourcePressure: Core process three: operations links strategy and people through fast budgeting, synchronization, sound assumptions, operating plans, trade-offs, contingencies, quarterly reviews, and goals.
chapters.coreMove: Synchronize resources, assumptions, trade-offs, and contingencies so the plan can move under real conditions.
chapters.commonMisread: Reduce operations to scheduling, productivity, or budget administration.

chapters.title: Conclusion: Letter to a New Leader
chapters.sourcePressure: Conclusion framed as direct counsel to a new leader: keep realism, people, strategy, operations, and follow-through linked without adding new doctrine.
chapters.coreMove: Carry the execution discipline as a daily leadership obligation after the first declaration fades.
chapters.commonMisread: Close with inspirational leadership generalities or sentimental advice.
